national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE); principal online portal: impots.gouv.fr and the business tax account (espace professionnel). VAT identification is administered through the French tax administration and, for intra-EU transactions, validated through the European Commission VIES system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS must be registered through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The filing is transmitted to the Registre national des entreprises and relevant tax and social authorities. The company receives a SIREN number, a SIRET establishment number and an APE activity code. The competent SIE assigns or confirms the French tax account and VAT status. A French VAT identification number generally consists of the country prefix FR, a two-character key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies to the non-resident tax service or the competent SIE, submits constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identification of representatives, bank and address information, and appoints a French tax representative where required. EU-established businesses generally do not need a French tax representative; non-EU businesses may require one for French VAT compliance, subject to applicable arrangements and exemptions. Registration should be completed before taxable French activities, intra-EU acquisitions, imports or other transactions requiring a French VAT number. Importers must also obtain an EORI number through French customs and ensure VAT representation in customs systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS) on its taxable profits. A qualifying SAS may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, or IR) for up to five fiscal years if statutory conditions are satisfied, including eligible ownership, activity, size and age requirements; the election is made with the tax administration within the prescribed period and is not a general check-the-box election. A qualifying family-owned company may use other statutory regimes only if its legal form and ownership satisfy the relevant conditions. France has no general US-style entity classification election. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive and French law can deny deductions, include income or neutralize mismatches involving transparent entities, instruments or permanent establishments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), supplemented by customs duties and excise rules. French VAT applies to taxable supplies made in France, intra-EU transactions, imports and certain cross-border services under place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold exempts a French manufacturing SAS from VAT registration when it carries out taxable transactions. The domestic VAT franchise regime may apply below the applicable annual turnover limits, generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory base-year and threshold rules and legislative changes. The franchise does not remove registration obligations arising from imports, intra-EU acquisitions, reverse-charge transactions or other specifically reportable operations. The EU-wide distance-sales threshold for qualifying intra-EU consumer sales is EUR 10,000 across the EU, subject to the One Stop Shop rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance system for all domestic business-to-business invoices. Mandatory electronic invoicing and transaction/payment-data reporting are being phased in through accredited private platforms connected to the public directory. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; large and medium-sized businesses must issue electronic invoices from that date, while small and micro-businesses generally become issuers from 1 September 2027. E-invoices must use an approved structured or hybrid format and contain required invoice, VAT and trading-party data. E-reporting applies to specified cross-border transactions and business-to-consumer transactions. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Customs declarations and import VAT data are processed through French customs systems, including electronic customs platforms, with EORI and MRN data where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT where the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU and the supplier retains legally acceptable evidence of export and exit. The supplier must identify the transaction correctly in its VAT records and VAT return. Direct exports require evidence linking the goods, supplier, customer, customs declaration and exit from the EU. Indirect exports may qualify where the purchaser or an authorized intermediary arranges transport and the statutory conditions are met. Intra-EU supplies of goods may be exempt from French VAT where the customer has a valid VAT identification number in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State and the supplier retains transport and reporting evidence. Services supplied to a business established outside France may fall outside French VAT under the business-to-business place-of-supply rule; this is generally not a zero-rated export and requires customer-status and place-of-use substantiation. Pharmaceutical and insulin products remain subject to ordinary VAT rules unless a specific statutory exemption, reduced rate or medical-supply rule applies; product classification must be confirmed separately.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration containing the Export Accompanying Document data and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs release and exit confirmation, such as the electronic exit results message or equivalent customs proof
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, Incoterm, destination and VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR or equivalent
Evidence linking the transport and goods to the customs declaration, including tracking or carrier confirmation where relevant
Proof of delivery or import clearance in the destination country where required to resolve evidentiary gaps
For intra-EU supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number, transport evidence and required recapitulative statement
Payment or bank evidence where commercially available; inward remittance certification is not generally a French statutory condition for export VAT exemption
For offshore services, customer establishment and VAT status evidence, contract, invoice, place-of-use analysis and proof that the service is supplied under the applicable business-to-business rule
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for export VAT exemption. The supplier must nevertheless maintain reliable evidence of export, transport, customer identity, transaction value and correct VAT treatment. If zero-rating is unsupported or incorrectly claimed, the DGFiP may assess the unpaid VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and applicable penalties. Common penalty levels include a 10% surcharge for certain late or deficient filings, 40% for deliberate failure, and up to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abusive conduct, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Incorrectly refunded or offset VAT may be recovered with interest and penalties. Serious tax fraud may trigger criminal proceedings, including imprisonment and fines under the French Tax Code, with aggravated sanctions for organized or concealed fraud. Customs violations may result in post-clearance recovery of duties and import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture of goods, and criminal liability where applicable. Export documentation, customs messages, invoices, transport records, accounting records and VAT returns should generally be retained for the applicable French statutory limitation and audit periods, commonly three years for VAT assessment, subject to extensions and special rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central banking authority for the French Republic) acting with the Direction Generale du Tresor (French Treasury, Ministry of Economy and Finance) as the competent authority for foreign exchange and capital movement policy, and the Autorite de Controle Prudentiel et de Resolution (ACPR) as the licensing and prudential supervisory authority for credit institutions, investment firms, and payment services providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a core Eurozone member; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible on both current and capital account without prior administrative authorisation, consistent with Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Profit remittance from the FR_SAS to non-resident shareholders is freely permitted once distributable reserves are evidenced and French corporate income tax (standard rate of 25% for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022) has been settled. Dividends to EU/EEA parent companies meeting the conditions of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU), including a minimum 10% holding or the 5% threshold where applicable, are exempt from French withholding tax. Dividends to non-EU treaty residents remain subject to the 25% flat-rate withholding (or the 30% single withholding levy (prelevement unique) where no treaty applies), subject to treaty reduction. There are no convertibility restrictions, no profit remittance licensing gates, and no administrative exchange approvals for genuine cross-border biopharmaceutical manufacturing and trading flows. However, Banque de France imposes purely statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations on all cross-border payments exceeding EUR 10,000 per transaction, and all foreign direct investment inflows into France remain declarable to the Direction Generale du Tresor for statistical and, where applicable, review purposes under the foreign investment screening regime (articles L151-1 et seq. of the Code Monetaire et Financier).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable under French law or the Eurozone legal framework. France does not operate an export proceeds surrender regime, does not impose mandatory conversion of export receipts into EUR, and does not require repatriation of export proceeds within any statutory timeline. The FR_SAS may retain USD, CNY, or other currency receivables from the export of recombinant human insulin in foreign-currency accounts at an authorised French credit institution. The sole ongoing obligations are: (i) statistical declaration to Banque de France of cross-border payment flows when the cumulative annual threshold or the per-transaction threshold (commonly EUR 10,000) is exceeded, and (ii) verification that the underlying export documentation (commercial invoice, EU GMP certificate, ANSM export licence, AWB or bill of lading, and customs export declaration) supports the receipt for AML/CFT and TRACFIN reporting purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance LC Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury / Medium for auxiliary payments. French-registered electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto and Shine may lawfully hold funds, issue French IBANs, and process SEPA transfers, but they are not credit institutions under the Code Monetaire et Financier and therefore cannot host capital escrow accounts, issue or confirm documentary letters of credit, provide sovereign health LC instruments, or act as correspondent for cross-border trade settlement. Non-EEA offshore digital EMIs (e.g., global FX wallets) are rated Low viability for this High_Risk_Special_License AML tier because their proof-of-funds documentation is generally rejected by French Tier-1 banks, they lack a licensed French branch, and the ACPR expects all high-risk pharmaceutical treasury flows to originate from a fully licensed EU payment service provider under PSD2. An auxiliary EMI integration is permissible solely for small remote vendor payments not exceeding EUR 10,000 per operation, provided the beneficiary is fully screened and a complete audit trail is retained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory requirement for physical presence exists; remote identification is legally permitted under Article R561-5-1 of the Code Monetaire et Financier and eIDAS Regulation (EU) 910/2014, either through a qualified electronic signature (QES) or ACPR-accredited video KYC. In practice, for a newly incorporated SAS classified as High_Risk_Special_License (ISIC 2100 recombinant biologicals), all relevant French Tier-1 banks de facto require: (i) physical appearance or notarially certified identity verification of the legal representative (President) at the account-opening interview; (ii) submission of the societe's RCS K-bis, articles of association, and JO-BODACC UBO filing; and (iii) a final face-to-face or QES-signed banking mandate (convention de compte) before the capital escrow account is activated. Non-resident directors may appoint a local director with an apostilled and legalized power of attorney (procuration), but the compliance interview cannot be delegated where a UBO or executive has been identified as high-risk; this effectively mandates a physical or QES-verified interview for the FR_SAS treasury structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First inbound capital injection of EUR 50,000 or more from a non-resident shareholder arriving before the SAS is fully operational, without a disclosed underlying corporate deed, creating a TRACFIN-reportable suspicion for a newly formed high-risk pharma entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the notarized deed of incorporation and capital increase (acte de souscription), the updated RCS K-bis, an organisation chart identifying all natural-person beneficial owners with 25%+ control, current 12-month bank statements of the shareholder entity, a signed letter of commitment from the UBOs explaining the economic purpose ('capital contribution for GMP build-out'), and a SWIFT MT103 remittance reference containing the ISO 20022 purpose code 'INCA' or 'CAPT'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership obscurity: a corporate shareholder registered in a non-EEA jurisdiction, or a trust/nominee structure holding more than 25% of the SAS, preventing completion of the French 'Beneficiaires Effectifs' (UBO) register filing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully completed JO-BODACC UBO declaration with official French translations of all foreign registry documents, certificate of good standing from the home commercial registry, identification of every nominee and discretionary trust beneficiary through a letter of engagement and underlying natural-person details, statutory declaration that no bearer shares or unregistered voting rights exist, and a written undertaking to notify the bank and the registry of any UBO change within 30 days as required by French AML law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank de-risking / shell company concern: the SAS is recently incorporated, has no audited French GAAP financial statements, no material local staff, and requests immediate opening of cross-border inbound and outbound trade facilities for insulin manufacture.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial lease (bail commercial) for French production premises, provisional or approved ANSM / EU GMP file (autorisation de fabrication or manufacturer's licence under the Public Health Code), URSSAF payroll registration with employment contracts for the local technical director and quality personnel, an initial-year business plan and budget reviewed by a French expert-comptable (registered accountant), and a capital commitment letter from a regulated parent holding entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sovereign health trade flow involving public procurement or state-owned recipient institutions, with possible politically exposed person (PEP) status of procurement officials, raising Sapin II anti-corruption and ABC (anti-bribery and corruption) screening flags in the 'Sovereign_Health_LC' payment rail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sovereign tender award or state health procurement contract with official English/French translation, a copy of the irrevocable documentary letter of credit (including the issuing bank's SWIFT header and expiry date), a Sapin II anti-corruption compliance certificate, a complete ABC risk assessment, bank references from the issuer's principal relationship bank, and a documented confirmation that no intermediaries, commission agents, or undisclosed distributors are engaged outside the disclosed distribution and supply agreement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections into the FR_SAS must be executed through the SWIFT MT103 channel (or a direct TARGET2/T2 entry) to the beneficiary's French IBAN (FR76 + BBAN + RIB key) at the nominated Tier-1 French bank. The SWIFT message must clearly carry the ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPT' (capital transfer) or 'INCA' (investment in capital), the full legal name and address of the sending entity, and a remittance reference matching the French capital increase deed. The receiving bank will treat the account as a blocked or escrow account (compte sequestre) until the following are physically or electronically delivered: (i) the RCS K-bis, (ii) the notarized capital increase decision, (iii) the completed JO-BODACC UBO declaration, and (iv) the source-of-funds dossier. There is no exchange-control authorization requirement for the injection, but the operation is subject to Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical reporting when the transaction exceeds EUR 10,000, and the sending bank must be fully AML-cleared with no sanctions exposure. Verified inbound funds become available for the GMP build-out and operating expenses only after the escrow conditions are lifted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For disbursements to EU suppliers of raw materials (yeast expression media, chromatography resins, sterile filtration consumables, analytical reagents), the primary clearing rail is the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for transactions up to EUR 100,000. For non-EU trade settlements in USD, GBP, CNY, or other currencies, the appropriate rail is SWIFT MT103 with field 50K (ordering customer), field 59 (beneficiary), and field 70 containing a structured purpose code such as 'TRAD' (trade) or 'PURP' (purchase and sale of goods); charges must be 'SHA' and all corporate identifiers must match the KYC records to avoid correspondent-bank rejections. For sovereign health sales under the 'Sovereign_Health_LC' rail, the FR_SAS must operate through an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued by the buyer's state bank and confirmed by a French or European confirmation bank, governed by UCP 600 and ISBP 745, with presentation of the pharmaceutical invoice, transport documents, EU GMP / ANSM export certificate, packing list, and any required phytosanitary or biological-material customs declarations. All outbound shipments must be declared through the French customs electronic system DELTA / GUN, with HS classification appropriate to recombinant human insulin API (NACE 21.10 / HS 2937.11 or 2941.90 as applicable), and counterparties must be screened against EU, UN, and French sanctions lists before each disbursement is released.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX purchase/sale contracts (change a terme ferme) for EUR/USD and EUR/CNH trade flows, maturity 1 to 12 months, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, restricted to underlying confirmed trade receivables and payables of the FR_SAS.
FX swaps (swap de change) to manage temporary EUR/USD liquidity mismatches arising from USD-denominated sovereign health LC collections and EUR-denominated operating costs.

Zero-cost collar and EUR/USD option strategies permitted for corporate counterparties under MiFID II, subject to the execution of a bank credit line, an internal hedging policy, and suitability documentation with the French Tier-1 provider.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited onshore deliverability (e.g., INR, EGP, VND) that appear in export tenders, permitted only where a genuine underlying trade exposure exists and the hedging rationale is documented and approved by the ACPR-regulated bank.

Cross-currency swaps (CIRS) for long-dated transformation of USD or CNY-denominated debt financing into the EUR functional currency of the French GMP facility, subject to EMIR clearing and trade reporting obligations where applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 225,000 for legal entities for non-publication or false declaration; possible suspension of marketing authorization for insulin products

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when an SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds for a financial year: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees > 50. Appointment is required for the following fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général under ANC règlements) as aligned with EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS only for consolidated statements of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO re-filing exists in France. The UBO declaration is required at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any ownership change. During the annual accounts deposit, the registry cross-checks UBO information and the SAS must confirm its accuracy; any unreported change is sanctioned as a false declaration. Legal entity fines: EUR 25,000; individual fines: EUR 5,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, potential imprisonment, and civil restitution orders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of corporate veil leading to personal liability for debts and taxes, possible travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment for willful non-compliance, and disqualification from management
